playbook_conclusion_A_vs_B.question: Does the chain FRAME buy anything beyond what shared references already give?
playbook_conclusion_A_vs_B.answer: YES — the chain frame buys the SEAM (same-moment continuation). Shared references carry CHARACTER + COSTUME + LOCATION identity (both arms hold those). Only the chain frame carries the EXACT END-STATE — pose, prop position (the bowler), camera angle, and precise grade — needed for a cut to read as a continuation of the same moment. ARM A's seam is continuous; ARM B's is a hard cut to a new moment.
playbook_conclusion_A_vs_B.trade_off: The chain-frame start-image slightly SUPPRESSES immediate crowd density: ARM A's Shot 2 working-crew was sparser than ARM B's, because the single-man start frame's composition propagates into the following shots.
playbook_conclusion_A_vs_B.recommendation: Use the chain frame when the cut must read as CONTINUOUS (mid-action continuation of the same moment). Use references-only when the next shot is a FRESH beat where only character/location continuity matters and fuller staging freedom is wanted. For 1a part-2 specifically: ARM A is the correct choice IF part-2 is meant to continue directly from part-1 Shot 5; ARM B is preferable if part-2 opens as a new beat.
